note: strong: honest about the risk, specific safeguards
text:
Dear Uncle Pono,

I found a studio apartment in Hilo that I really want, but the landlord requires a co-signer because my income is a little under three times the rent. Co-signing means you would be legally responsible for the rent if I could not pay, so I want to be honest about my plan before you decide.

I made a budget that covers rent every month with money left for food, gas and my phone. I will set up autopay on payday, keep an emergency fund equal to one month of rent in savings, and share my bank statement with you each month.

I know this is a big favor. I respect you, and I am grateful that you would even consider it. Thank you for trusting me.

With love and respect,
Keoni

Dear Mom,

I am asking if you would be willing to co-sign the lease for the apartment near my work. The landlord needs a co-signer because this is my first apartment and I have no rental history yet.

I want you to understand what this means: if I miss a payment, you would have to pay it. I do not want that to ever happen, so here is my plan. My paycheck covers the rent with about four hundred dollars left each month. I already have savings as a cushion, I will use automatic payments, and I will show you my budget whenever you ask.

I appreciate everything you have done for me. Thank you for thinking about this.

Love,
Maile

text:
Dear Grandma Lani,

I want to ask you something important. I found a shared house with two roommates, but the landlord says I need a co-signer because my income is low right now. If you co-sign, it means you would have to pay my part of the rent if I can't.

Here is my plan so that never happens. I made a budget and I will pay rent first every month. I have savings for emergencies and I will set up autopay. I will also show you my budget every month so you know I am on track.

I love you and I really appreciate you. Thank you for even thinking about it.

Love,
Kalena

Dear Aunty Mele,

I hope you are doing well. I am writing to ask whether you would be willing to co-sign my lease. The property manager requires a co-signer because my income is just below their limit.

Co-signing is a real responsibility. If I could not pay, you would be responsible for the rent, and it could affect your credit. I take that seriously. My plan is simple: rent comes out of my paycheck by autopay, I keep two months of rent in an emergency fund, and I will share my monthly statements with you.

Whatever you decide, I respect it, and I am grateful for all your support over the years. Mahalo for reading this.

With gratitude,
Isaiah
